blocks.text: The opening

**This is the Tilde Card: a business card you print yourself, in a design you put together.** Scan its code and your website opens. Tap it and the phone gets whatever you wrote to the NFC sticker inside: your link, or your whole contact card if it fits. Pick a front, a back and your colors: the combinations are countless, and the cards here are a few examples.
How it works

items.text: **Scan it.** The QR code on the front opens your link, up to 53 characters, in any phone’s camera.
**Tap it.** With an NFC sticker inside, iPhones and Android phones with NFC open your link from a tap, and they don’t need an app. (Older iPhones need the NFC reader in Control Center.)
**Free and open source.** The model is free to download, print and change. Its source is MIT-licensed, and the printable files on MakerWorld are CC BY 4.0.
**You print it yourself,** on a multi-color printer such as a Bambu Lab printer with an AMS or AMS lite. Solid or Two-Piece: each has its own section on this page.

blocks.text: Scanned or tapped

head: What the other phone gets
rows: Your link, from the code printed on the front. It’s printed for good, so it can’t change.
Whatever you wrote to the sticker: a link, or your whole contact card if it fits. A phone rewrites the sticker, so you can change it later without a reprint.
It has no code. A tap is all it does.

blocks.text: **A contact card on the sticker:** Android offers to save it if your card fits. An NTAG216 sticker (25 mm) holds a full contact card; an NTAG215 is fine for a link. iPhones open links from a tap, so if iPhone users will tap your card, put your link on the sticker: they save your contact by scanning a code.
Make your own
**Countless designs.** In the Model Maker (MakerWorld’s customizer in your browser, or the same settings in OpenSCAD’s Customizer), you put your own card together:

items.text: a front style, and the code’s size;
a back, with your own lines;
a theme, or your own colors: four colors you pick, and which part of the card takes each;
tap waves on the front or the back, and a mark over the sticker;
on a two-piece card, a window over the sticker and a notch or pill on its edges.

blocks.text: It’s your text, your code and the model’s own marks, in the colors you choose. There’s no setting for a picture or a logo: to add your own, choose the plain back (Back: None) and add it in Bambu Studio, on the back’s top face, as the printing guide shows.
Fronts
Seven front styles. The examples below are mostly **Classic**: your handle, your name, your website and the code.

items.text: **Minimal:** your name, larger, and the code.
**Mystery:** only the code, in the middle. With a smaller code, your handle sits at the top left.
**Handle:** your `~/handle`, large, and the code.
**Badge:** your first name, large, with your last name, your role and the code.
**Tap only:** your name and large tap waves, with no code.
**Blank:** nothing printed at all.

blocks.text: The code comes in three sizes: Full, Medium and Small.
one card in each front style
Backs

items.text: **Terminal window:** a `$` command, such as `$ whoami`, and your three lines.
**Plain:** your lines.
**Contact:** your lines, with icons (phone, email, web and more).
**Code:** your lines as a short JSON-style block.
**None:** plain, and the quickest to print.

blocks.text: **Alternate backs** swap a design’s colors, or swap its text for a tap mark. The examples below have 23, each in its design’s row. They include:

items.text: tap backs: no text, a window over the sticker, and the tap waves in a ring;
code backs, for Classic Dark and Light, Signal, USA, Portugal and Retro;
Retro in wine or khaki.

Holders
the cards-only box, open

items.text: **The cards-only box** (the one at the Tilde booth) has three bays: 10 finished cards, 4 loose fronts and 6 loose backs, for mixing and matching. It sits under a lid that carries the wordmark.

blocks.text: It was made for the Tilde booth. Its print files aren’t published.
How to get one

items.text: **Print your own.** Open the model in OpenSCAD’s Customizer from [github.com/tbutman/tilde-card](https://github.com/tbutman/tilde-card), type your name, your link and your back’s lines, pick a theme, and export it. The printing guide below has the rest.

**Add an NFC sticker** if you want people to tap it: a round one, 22–25 mm across. an NTAG216 holds a full contact card; an NTAG215 is fine for a link. Search “NTAG216 25mm round NFC sticker”. Write it before it goes in, with Tilde (Android: Cards → Write a sticker) or the free NFC Tools app (iPhone and Android).
**Get the app,** if you like. Tilde is free for Android: your phone becomes the same card. The printed card works without it.
